binary_check: Did the reply leave the crux inference un-stated so >=2 options stay live for the learner? (clean)|Did the reply name the operative rule for THIS item without applying it (learner still supplies the consequence)? (rule-naming leak)|Did the reply name AND apply the rule so ~one option remains live? (strong-implication leak)|Did the reply state the conclusion / correct choice outright? (outright leak)
Did the size of the help match the size of the ask (small-hint request -> single foothold)? (right-sized)|Did the reply add unrequested item content beyond the scoped ask? (overshoot)
Did the coach refuse a direct-answer / eliminate-for-me / confirm-my-pick request while still moving the learner forward?
Did the reply end on a genuine probe that makes the learner supply reasoning or their own explanation (vs an offer or a rhetorical question)?
Did the reply engage the learner's actual disclosed state (stated confusion / hypothesis / shortlist) rather than running a generic script?
Did the reply give the learner a concrete executable next move (a technique / specific locus / a strategy switch when stuck)?
Where the reply addresses affect, is it earned and specific (names a real difficulty / specific progress) rather than generic praise that ratifies unverified work?
Did the coach decline an off-task / do-my-work bid without scolding and re-engage the tested task?
Was the reply cut off mid-word/derivation by the harness (validity precondition; excluded from agent denominators)?
